record.paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
record.original_question: Fix a pair of vertices in a graph G. Is the number of interlacing values for resolvent centrality always less than or equal to the number of interlacing values for exponential subgraph centrality? Here the comparison is between the number of parameter values α for which [(I − αA)^{-1}]_{ii} = [(I − αA)^{-1}]_{jj} and the number of parameter values β for which [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj}.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. For a given pair of vertices of a graph G, prove or disprove the following statement: the number of interlacing values relative to resolvent centrality is always less than or equal to the number of interlacing values relative to subgraph centrality.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix $A$. For a real parameter $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|<1/\rho(A)$ (where $\rho(A)$ is the spectral radius of $A$), the resolvent subgraph centrality of vertex $i$ is the diagonal entry $[(I-\alpha A)^{-1}]_{ii}$. For a real parameter $\beta>0$, the exponential subgraph centrality of vertex $i$ is the diagonal entry $[e^{\beta A}]_{ii}$.

Fix two distinct vertices $i,j\in V$. Define
\[ N_R(i,j) = \#\{\alpha\in(-1/\rho(A),\,1/\rho(A)) : [(I-\alpha A)^{-1}]_{ii} = [(I-\alpha A)^{-1}]_{jj}\}, \]
\[ N_E(i,j) = \#\{\beta\in(0,\infty) : [e^{\beta A}]_{ii} = [e^{\beta A}]_{jj}\}. \]
These are called the numbers of interlacing values of resolvent centrality and of exponential subgraph centrality for the pair $(i,j)$, respectively.

Prove or disprove: for every finite simple graph $G$ and every pair of vertices $i,j$, one has
\[ N_R(i,j) \le N_E(i,j). \]
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in the work introducing it (2021/2023). A web search reveals no later paper resolving the inequality between numbers of interlacing values of resolvent and exponential subgraph centralities for general simple graphs. Related results discuss matching between exponential- and resolvent-based centralities but do not settle this comparison.

status_evidence.title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on subgraph centrality including comparison of interlacing values between resolvent and exponential centrality.
status_evidence.claim: The comparison is explicitly stated as an unresolved problem.

status_evidence.title: Matching exponential-based and resolvent-based centrality measures
status_evidence.snippet: Studies correspondences between resolvent- and exponential-based centrality measures without resolving the interlacing count inequality.
status_evidence.claim: No proof of the inequality N_R <= N_E is given in this related work.
